One is about the U.S. trade deficit; the other is an issue that could become the greatest technology war i Carter's baby 'penguin' outfit recalled
A three-piece outfit for infants and toddlers is being recalled because one of the buttons can pull off and create a potential choking hazard, the Consumer Product Safety Commission said.
The commission said it has become aware of three instances in which children were found to have the buttons in their mouths, though no injuries were reported. More than 107,000 of the Chinese-made sets were sold in the U.S.
The cardigan set with a penguin embroidered on the shirt was sold under the Carter’s brand. The brand is part of William B. Carter, an Atlanta-based operation that bills itself as the nation’s largest marketer of baby and children’s clothing. It also owns the OshKosh B’gosh brand.
The “three-piece penguin cardigan set” has the white bodysuit, gray cardigan top with a hood and matching pants. They were sold in sizes intended for newborns to 2-year-olds.

They were sold not only in Carter’s stores, but Bon-Ton, Burlington Stores, Kohls, Macys, Ross Stores, Toys R Us, and elsewhere through March. They cost about $40. The commission said anyone who has the sets should return to a Carter’s store, or reach Carter’s online through its consumer help center, for a refund in the form of a gift card.
